groups.title: Database Integration Patterns
groups.question: You are adding PostgreSQL with Drizzle to your Nuxt app and the schema will evolve. Explain how Drizzle defines the schema and changes the database.

followUps.Drizzle ORM Schema Definition: How does Drizzle define a schema and give you typed queries?
followUps.Drizzle Migrations Workflow: How does Drizzle's migration workflow work?

evidence.text: The schema is written in TypeScript as table definitions.
Query types are inferred from it without a code generation step.
The schema is the single source of truth for the database structure.

notEnough: Only saying Drizzle is an ORM.

evidence.text: drizzle-kit generate writes SQL migration files from schema changes.
drizzle-kit migrate applies them to the database.
The generated SQL should be reviewed before applying it.

groups.title: PostgreSQL Fundamentals
groups.question: Your serverless deployment runs out of database connections, and creating a user plus their profile sometimes leaves half-saved data. Explain pooling and transactions.

followUps.Connection Pooling in Serverless Environ: Why do serverless functions exhaust PostgreSQL connections?
followUps.Transactions and ACID Guarantees: How do transactions prevent half-saved data?

evidence.text: Database connections are costly and limited.
Many short-lived function instances each open their own connections.
A connection pooler or a serverless-friendly driver shares a small number of connections.
A transaction groups operations so they all succeed or all fail.
If one step fails, the earlier ones are rolled back.
Transactions also isolate concurrent work and keep data consistent.

groups.title: Nuxt and Database Architecture
groups.question: You are building a multi-tenant SaaS on Nuxt where each company's data must stay separate. Explain how you would set up the database client and enforce isolation.

followUps.Database Client Singleton Pattern: How do you share one database client across server routes?
followUps.Row-Level Security and Multi-tenancy: How does Row-Level Security protect tenants?

evidence.text: Modules are cached, so a client created in one file is shared when imported.
One client is created and reused across routes.
Creating a client per request wastes connections.

notEnough: Only saying you use a singleton.

evidence.text: Row-Level Security policies limit which rows a session can see.
The database enforces them even if application code forgets a filter.
It is a second layer of protection on top of application checks.

groups.title: Query Optimization
groups.question: Your posts page makes a query per author, and filtering orders by customer gets slower every month. Explain how you would fix both.

followUps.N+1 Query Problem with Drizzle: What is the N+1 problem here and how would you fix it with Drizzle?

evidence.text: Fetching a list, then a query per item for related data, makes many queries.
A join or relational query loads related data together.
This turns many queries into one or two.
Columns used in WHERE, ORDER BY and joins are good index candidates.
Without indexes, the database scans the whole table.
Indexes slow writes slightly, so add them for real query patterns.
